tier_reason: The README Overview gives only first-party absolute figures (5-20 ns MPHF query, 2.10-2.71 bits/key). It shows no baseline row, no CPU and no compiler. The public criterion code in benches/mphf.rs records the source runs (N=1M random u64) but has no baseline either. The only head-to-head numbers anywhere are third-party, in unmerged PR #6, with no hardware stated. They show no clear win over std, so C is the ceiling.

corrections.baseline: Rust std::collections::HashMap / HashSet, tested only in the third-party benches of unmerged PR #6 (with FxHash and with the SipHash DefaultHasher). The README itself claims, without numbers, faster query and construction than the `ph` crate (beling/bsuccinct-rs) and better performance than rkyv::ArchivedHashMap. std::unordered_map is never tested.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README (first-party, no baseline row): Mphf query time 5-20 ns depending on parameters, number of keys and L1-L3 cache sizes; 2.10-2.71 bits/key. benches/mphf.rs doc comment (N=1M random u64, Mphf<32,8>): 14.372 ms per 1M gets at gamma 1.0 (2.10 bits/key) and 4.5959 ms at gamma 2.0 (2.72 bits/key), i.e. ~14.4 and ~4.6 ns/get (derived from page data). No first-party head-to-head against any baseline. Third-party unmerged PR #6 (result black_box fixed, N=1M u64, hardware unstated): Mphf get 26.267 ms (gamma 1.0) / 19.683 ms (gamma 2.0) per 1M; Set contains 26.454 ms vs std HashSet+FxHash 14.704 ms (~1.8x slower) and vs std HashSet+DefaultHasher (SipHash) 34.877 ms (~1.32x faster; ~1.06x at equal hasher, 32.839 ms); u64->u32 get: new Map 37.293 ms and MapWithDict 45.406 ms vs std HashMap+FxHash 18.518 / 18.921 ms (~2.0x / ~2.4x slower); archived Map get 41.039 ms vs rkyv ArchivedHashMap 37.373 ms (~1.1x slower). All ratios derived from page data.
corrections.workload: First-party: Mphf::get latency and bits/key for Mphf<32,8> over 1M random u64 keys at gamma 1.0 and 2.0 (benches/mphf.rs). The README's 5-20 ns covers the bare MPHF only, not map or set lookups; benches/map_with_dict.rs records 75.814 ms per 1M MapWithDict<u64,u32> gets (~75.8 ns each, derived). Third-party PR #6: Set::contains and Map/MapWithDict get over 1M random u64 keys with u32 values, against Rust std HashMap/HashSet (FxHash and SipHash DefaultHasher) and rkyv 0.8 ArchivedHashMap.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc version not stated. Cargo.toml [profile.release], which the bench profile inherits: opt-level=3, lto="fat", codegen-units=1, debug=true. No target-cpu or RUSTFLAGS stated. Third-party PR #6 comments out these release settings, so its numbers use Cargo defaults.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 45 GitHub stars; crates.io v1.2.0 with 839,098 total downloads (213,123 recent); 1 public reverse dependency (simd-lookup). Cloudflare-owned; commit history references internal BOTS/BOTSML tickets.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers are absolute only: the README and the benches/*.rs doc comments state no CPU, OS, rustc version or baseline row. The README's 5-20 ns is for the bare Mphf::get, not for MapWithDict or Set lookups (~75.8 ns per MapWithDict get in the repo's own bench comment, derived). The original benches black_box only the key and do not black_box the result. Unmerged third-party PR #6 fixes this and measures 19.7-26.3 ns per Mphf get instead of 4.6-14.4 ns (hardware unstated, fat-LTO profile disabled, so not a like-for-like rerun). benches/set.rs has a std HashSet harness but publishes no results, and it still uses the fxhash crate that was removed from Cargo.toml in 2024-10 (issue #5), so it likely does not build as-is. The claimed wins over the ph crate and rkyv::ArchivedHashMap have no numbers; PR #6 (rkyv 0.8) shows the archived entropy map ~1.1x slower than rkyv ArchivedHashMap, and its author comments that ArchivedHashMap was faster in real usage. Against Rust std, PR #6 shows entropy-map ~1.8-2.4x slower with FxHash and ~1.3x faster only against the default SipHash HashSet (~1.06x at equal hasher). The real advantage is memory (2.10-2.72 bits/key for the MPHF). No C++ baseline was tested. GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION because LICENSE is the short Apache-2.0 notice; Cargo.toml declares Apache-2.0.

notes: Borderline reject (not-faster): the only head-to-head data (third-party PR #6) show entropy-map slower than Rust std HashMap/HashSet with FxHash and slower than rkyv ArchivedHashMap, faster only against std's default SipHash HashSet, mostly from the hasher. I kept it as a downgrade because the README does claim faster queries than ph and it has 839k crates.io downloads; its real edge is memory, not latency. Metadata checks out: Apache-2.0 (NOASSERTION on GitHub, Apache-2.0 in the LICENSE notice and Cargo.toml), 45 stars, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-09-09 (active).
